summary: Intro discovery call focused on p95 latency targets, concurrency and streaming behavior for Arcadia Commerce's conversational agents. Customer is evaluating hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) and cares about p95 under 400ms for short prompts and 1.5s for long streaming sessions at 25 concurrent users plus burst. Action items: run benchmarks, share security docs, price tiers, schedule POC kickoff.
transcript:
Header: 2026-08-05 15:00 UTC | Duration 43 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Head of ML, Arcadia), Jordan Lee (CTO, Arcadia), Samir Khan (Infra Eng, Arcadia)

00:00 Sofia: Hey everyone thanks for taking the time. we wanted to cover your latency and throughput targets and talk about options hosted vs dedicated vs private and what a POC would look like.
00:18 Maya: Thanks Sofia. to set context, Arcadia runs conversational assistants across our commerce site - search summarization, cart suggestions, and a small support bot. our biggest constraint right now is p95 latency under load, and also cost.
00:30 Jordan: right, to add - infra team wants to avoid big surprises with tokens/sec and autoscaling. we currently have a 25 concurrent user baseline for peak flows, with 2-3x burst.
00:45 Ethan: got it. quick question — are you using streaming responses in product or full-response only? that changes kernel and kv cache behavior.
00:54 Maya: yes we stream for the support bot and for product descriptions. streaming with low tail latency is critical; for short prompts we target p95 under 400ms, for longer streaming sessions (multi-turn) we expect p95 under 1.5s while sustaining ~6-8 tokens/sec per session.
01:15 Samir: and on concurrency, the 25 concurrent is realistic, but on sale days we see bursts to ~70-80 concurrent for short windows. we prefer graceful degradation rather than timeouts.
01:28 Sofia: that makes sense. for those targets we typically recommend looking at two levers: model size/quantization and deployment type. hosted can hit low latency for smaller models and bursty traffic via autoscaling; dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity so you get stable p95 at scale; private lets you keep data in your VPC and integrate with KMS for key rotation.
01:48 Jordan: what model sizes are you thinking? we're experimenting with a 13B base and testing 70B for higher-quality generations.
01:55 Ethan: common pattern we see: 13B quantized (8-bit) to hit sub-400ms p95 for single-turn short prompts on high-end A100 or equivalent; 70B tends to be higher latency but you can improve throughput with batching and our streaming kernel optimizations. our continuous-batching and KV cache also lower per-token cost for multi-turn flows.
02:20 Maya: can you explain the streaming kernel differences? we need to understand p95 behavior when tokens are emitted slowly vs fast.
02:28 Ethan: sure. streaming kernels minimize tail latency by optimizing small-token generation paths and by keeping KV cache locally pinned to the process so subsequent tokens don't incur extra scheduling overhead. there are tradeoffs - models and quantization affect per-token compute, while batching affects latency for first token. we tune for low-quantile latency by limiting batch windows for interactive flows.
03:00 Sofia: to give you a concrete benchmark we can run: 1k representative conversations, three prompt length buckets (short 20 tokens, mid 150 tokens, long 800 tokens), measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec under 25 and 75 concurrent. we'll run 13B FP16, 13B 8-bit, and a 70B 8-bit candidate.
03:18 Maya: perfect. and please include streaming on for the mid and long buckets — we want to see p95 for the first token and then steady-state tokens/sec.
03:28 Samir: also include KV-cache hit rates. we use repeated context across turns, so cache effectiveness is important.
03:34 Ethan: noted. we'll include prefix/KV cache scenarios and show how effective caching reduces end-to-end latency.
03:40 Jordan: on network topology, if we go private/VPC, does Redwood support private peering? we can't route traffic over the public internet for sensitive flows.
03:48 Sofia: yes - Redwood Private supports VPC peering and dedicated connectivity options, plus customer-managed KMS/HSM. that said, private deployments require longer lead times and an enterprise contract. Dedicated reserved capacity is often a middle ground - you get reserved GPUs and dedicated tenancy without full private control plane.
04:04 Maya: what's the typical autoscaling behavior on Hosted? how quickly can it pick up from 25 to 80 concurrent?
04:12 Ethan: hosted autoscaling is reactive - you get burst capacity but there can be short warm-up windows. for very spiky workloads, Dedicated with burst buffer or a hybrid routing policy (route to dedicated first, fallback to compatible hosted when saturated) gives best user experience. we can instrument routing policies per route.
04:33 Jordan: curious about cost tradeoffs - do you have ballpark per-token costs for the 13B vs 70B in hosted vs dedicated?
04:40 Sofia: we will share a pricing sheet; high level: hosted per-token is higher but operationally simpler; dedicated reduces unit cost at commit levels. we'll send preliminary pricing for the tiers relevant to your throughput.
04:55 Maya: on quality - if we quantize 13B to 8-bit, how much regression do you expect? we can't accept notable quality drop on product descriptions.
05:03 Ethan: there can be some differences; we recommend running evals on your prompt set. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles per workload and flag regressions via evals. part of the POC typically includes a quality gate on your dev prompts.
05:22 Samir: for the benchmark, what exact infra do you need from our side? we want to control traffic shape and replicate bursty windows.
05:29 Ethan: best is you provide a representative prompt set and concurrency profiles. we will run the workloads from our infra and can also share a synthetic harness so you can reproduce on-prem later. we'll include both steady-state and spike tests.
05:45 Maya: great. for security, we need SOC2 type II, SSO (SAML/SCIM), audit logs, and KMS integration. also data retention policy - we need logs not stored beyond 30 days.
05:56 Sofia: yes, we'll include SOC2 and ISO docs and outline retention and customer-controlled keys. our hosted product can be configured with short retention and encryption-at-rest; Private and Dedicated give you more control over retention and keys.
06:12 Jordan: can you support region pinning? we need EU region for some flows.
06:16 Ethan: region pinning is supported for Dedicated and Private; hosted has multi-region endpoints with region selection but for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private.
06:26 Samir: okay, let's align on POC acceptance criteria - what would you propose?
06:32 Sofia: typical acceptance criteria: p95 under your targets for the chosen model/config on 25 concurrent with acceptable degradation at 75 concurrent; no functional/regression failures on your eval prompts; successful KMS/SAML integration demo or documented integration plan; and an agreed cost estimate.
06:47 Maya: that sounds reasonable. can you give an estimate timeline?
06:50 Sofia: we can run initial benchmarks in ~5 business days if you share prompts and traffic shapes; POC kickoff could be the week of 2026-08-17. Private deployment discussions and legal review might add 4-6 weeks.
07:03 Jordan: about streaming latency numbers - do you have example numbers for 13B quantized on A100 under 25 concurrent? curious about first-token p95 and steady-state tokens/sec.
07:12 Ethan: from prior benchmarks: 13B 8-bit on modern A100s often yields first-token p95 ~280-380ms for short prompts, steady-state ~12-18 tokens/sec per session depending on sequence length and batching; 70B might be first-token p95 ~900-1200ms and steady-state lower, but batching and optimized kernels can push tokens/sec higher. we'll reproduce these numbers on your prompt set.
07:42 Maya: those are promising. we need to weigh quality vs latency; we may accept 70B for high-value flows and 13B for daytime traffic.
07:52 Sofia: that's a common hybrid approach - route high-value sessions to higher-quality models and low-latency flows to smaller models. Redwood's smart routing can handle fallbacks and A/Bs.
08:03 Samir: one more infra question - can we do canary rollouts and traffic mirroring for model rollouts? we need to validate model changes without impacting users.
08:11 Ethan: yes, rollouts, canaries, and traffic mirroring are built into the Console. you can do percentage rollouts by model version, run shadow traffic, and gather eval metrics.
08:22 Jordan: ok. sounds like next step is getting that benchmark run.
08:25 Sofia: we'll run the benchmark and share raw results plus a summary and recommendations. we'll also send the security pack and preliminary pricing.
08:33 Maya: thanks everyone.
08:36 Jordan: thanks.
08:38 Sofia: quick recap of action items - Ethan will run benchmarks, Sofia will send security/pricing, Maya will share prompts. we'll aim to reconvene after the benchmark.
08:49 Meeting end.
